scenarios.title: Walmart · pantry SKU (steady, ~12/day)
scenarios.description: Steady mid-volume pantry item at Walmart Los Angeles (item FOODS_1_218, store CA_3, roughly 12 units/day, about 5% zero-days). A good default; there's enough volume for clean statistics, and it's small enough that the reorder policy actually matters.

scenarios.title: Walmart · hobbies (very sparse)
scenarios.description: Very sparse demand at Walmart LA (item HOBBIES_2_017, store CA_3). Roughly 85% zero-days, around 0.2 units/day on average. A good real-world test for intermittent demand, where cycle service level and fill rate can diverge sharply.

scenarios.title: UK e-commerce · gift item (heavy-tailed)
scenarios.description: UK gift-shop item (StockCode 85123A, white hanging heart t-light holder) from UCI Online Retail II, 2009 through 2011. Heavy-tailed demand: the median is around 88 units/day, but the occasional 4,000-unit spike shows up. Cycle service level plateaus around 93 to 94% (95% isn't reachable), while fill rate stays near 100%. It's a good example of why fill rate often matters more than CSL on real retail data.
